item.title: 3 Observations from Indiana men’s basketball’s 90-76 win over Kentucky
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 20: Markus Burton #5 of the Indiana Hoosiers celebrates in the second half of the 90-76 win over the Kentucky Wildcats at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 20, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Darian DeVries avenged his loss to Kentucky last season with a 14-point win in the rivalry series’ ‘semi-neutral’ game at Lucas Oil Stadium. Indiana remains perfect on the season while the Wildcats fall to 4-2 with lopsided losses to both high major programs they’ve seen this year. Indiana built an early lead in the game before Milan Momcilovic single-handedly brought Kentucky back from the dead. His 22-point first half was enough to kill Indiana’s momentum and give Kentucky a two point lead heading into halftime. DeVries knew that the key to the second half would be slowing him down and his group came out and did just that. Momcilovic didn’t make a three in the entire second half and Indiana finally built the lead that eluded them early in the game, eventually winning 90-76. Here are three observations from the game: Bryce Lindsay It’s not often that your most important player is a bench guy, but Bryce Lindsay is looking like the best sixth-man in the country and has been a huge difference-maker for Indiana’s perfect start. It starts with his willingness to come off the bench. Lindsay started all 31 games at Villanova last season and clearly has the ability to be a high-major starter. Whatever the conversation was to get him to accept this role at Indiana, the fit is a testament to both he and DeVries. Part of what has made this work so well is that he tends to share the floor with one of Darren Harris or Markus Burton, allowing him to alternate between shooter and driver. The other part of it is simply his ability to hit shots at all levels, often with more than one defender on him. His 3-point shooting will always be what jumps off the page, especially with the range he showed against Arkansas, but tonight showed his versatility inside. Kentucky knew it struggled to defend the perimeter, so he punished their overly aggressive close-outs with drives or by drawing fouls from beyond the arc. He’s going to miss some frustrating ones with the green light he has, but Lindsay has shown a willingness and ability to hit the hardest shots all over the floor. This is an invaluable piece to have coming off the bench. Versatility I’ve been waiting for this team to establish either an interior or perimeter offensive identity this season, but it turns out Indiana’s real strength might be its ability to do both. DeVries knew that he had the size and experience over Arkansas inside and fed Samet Yigitoglu and Aiden Sherrell inside accordingly. Malachi Moreno negated that advantage against Kentucky, so DeVries fell back on the guard play that helped him beat Syracuse. item.title: The Prediction: Indiana Hoosiers
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, INDIANA - OCTOBER 26: Keleki Latu #85 of the Washington Huskies makes a catch against the Indiana Hoosiers at Memorial Stadium on October 26, 2024 in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tomorrow afternoon, the Huskies will welcome the defending national champ, Indiana, to Montlake as they search for an upset against the number 9 team in the land. Our staff has their picks below! Andrew Berg (5-4 SU, 4-5 ATS) The Huskies return home after a successful road trip in a week where 7/9 Big 10 home teams are underdogs. Of course, the Dawgs have not lit the world on fire at home this year, losing to Minnesota, Iowa, and Penn St at Husky Stadium (naming rights deal be damned, I will continue to say Husky Stadium). Indiana is the defending National Champions but has not looked as dominant as they did a year ago. In fact, they changed QBs to Grant Wilson last week against USC and the 6th year Old Dominion transfer looked rock solid. In fact, that game was a bounce-back of sorts for Indiana, who struggled to beat Michigan and Minnesota in the two previous games. Regardless of who plays QB, the RB duo of Beebe and Richard has kept the offense moving all season. The Husky defense has forced opponents to drive the length of the field and avoid making mistakes. It has worked for most of the season and led to lots of forced turnovers. Indiana has been disciplined and physical enough to avoid those mistakes, so it could be a tough game for the defense to make big plays. And that’s the side of the ball where the Huskies have more often had the advantage this year. The Husky offense had a strong first half against Michigan St last week, albeit only to the tune of 14 points on the board. Demond Williams finally looked like the QB from 2025 who trusted his arm to make difficult throws to talented receivers. Chris Lawson was primarily responsible for another win and has emerged as the standout skill-position player on the team. All the same, Indiana’s defense has been rock solid all year. They stymie teams who run the ball much better than the Huskies, so it is likely to be another one-dimensional attack. I don’t think UW will be anywhere close to being shut out at home, but I don’t think they can score enough to keep this one within reach. Indiana 30 – Washington 17 Luke Kemper (1-0 SU, 0-1 ATS) Unfortunately I think this is going to be a lopsided game and feel like the first half of the Iowa and Penn State games. The only difference is that Indiana will get it done through the air instead of on the ground. Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh are easily the best receiving duo that UW will have faced all year. After giving up chunk plays last week to Michigan State, one of the worst offenses in the country in that category, it is a big concern going into the game. item.title: No. 15 Vanderbilt Handles Business to Stay Undefeated
item.description: Photo by: ANDREW NELLES Vanderbilt continued its impressive start to the 2026-27 basketball season Friday night, defeating UCF 82-74 at Memorial Gymnasium in Nashville. The Commodores used a strong first half performance and timely scoring down the stretch to take care of a difficult opponent and improve to 6-0. Coming into the matchup, Vanderbilt was ranked No. 15 nationally and had looked dominant through its first five games. UCF presented a tougher challenge, entering Nashville with a 4-1 record and one of the nation’s most productive scorers in Dior Johnson. The Knights were hoping to earn a major road victory, but Vanderbilt quickly showed why it has become one of the teams to watch early in the season. Vanderbilt Builds an Early Advantage The Commodores came out with plenty of energy, taking control of the opening half with an efficient offensive performance. Vanderbilt found ways to attack the basket, move the ball and create scoring opportunities while making life difficult for UCF on the other end. Tyler Tanner played an important role in the early success, providing scoring and helping Vanderbilt establish control. His ability to contribute offensively and create opportunities for teammates gave the Commodores an important advantage. UCF struggled to find its shooting rhythm. The Knights had difficulty getting consistent production from the field, allowing Vanderbilt to build separation on the scoreboard. The Commodores carried a 38-29 advantage into halftime, putting themselves in a strong position heading into the final 20 minutes. Knights Make a Push, but Vanderbilt Responds UCF came out looking to make things interesting in the second half. The Knights increased their offensive production, scoring 45 points after halftime compared to 29 in the opening period. Dior Johnson continued to be an important part of the UCF offense, but the Knights needed more consistent contributions from the rest of the lineup to complete the comeback. Vanderbilt also remained productive offensively, adding 44 second-half points to keep UCF from getting within striking distance. Whenever the Knights looked capable of building momentum, the Commodores found ways to answer. That ability to respond ultimately made the difference. Vanderbilt did not allow UCF’s improved second-half offense to erase the advantage it had created before the break. Commodores Improve to 6-0 The final buzzer confirmed an 82-74 Vanderbilt victory. The eight-point win moves the Commodores to 6-0, while UCF falls to 4-2. The result gives Vanderbilt another important victory against a power-conference opponent and continues its strong opening stretch. The Commodores have demonstrated that they can win comfortably, but Friday’s contest also showed they can handle a more competitive game when an opponent makes a second-half push. item.title: MVP, box score, and Twitter reactions to Kentucky Wildcats’ loss to Indiana
item.description: Heading into halftime, Kentucky Basketball had as much momentum as they have had at any point in any game all season. The Wildcats closed the half on a 12-0 run to lead Indiana 47-45 at halftime inside Lucas Oil Stadium. Milan Momcilovic was making it rain, and Kentucky’s defense was getting stops. Then, the script completely flipped in the second half. Kentucky’s defense couldn’t stop fouling, and the Wildcats’ offense couldn’t stop turning the ball over. It led to a frustrating second half where Indiana gradually and frustratingly pulled away for a 90-76 win. The curse in Indianapolis continues for the Cats. Kentucky is now 4-2 on the season and 0-2 against Power Four teams. Next up for the Cats: A home game next Friday night against Wichita State. MVP: Milan Momcilovic Easy. Momcilovic exploded for 22 points and five three-pointers in the first half. He finished with a game-high 28 points. He can shoot, clearly. Now we just need to see it in a Kentucky uniform for 40 minutes in a Power Four game. Box Score First Half It was an offensive explosion on both sides early. The first media timeout didn’t come until 12:50 left in the first half. By that point, it was 19-19. Both teams were 8-14 from the floor, with a combined 5-8 from three-point range. Kentucky had five assists to no turnovers in the first 7:10 of the game, and Milan Momcilovic had seven points and two three-pointers. From there, though, Indiana kept up their shot-making, hitting six-of-eight to stretch out an 11-point lead to 36-25. Part of that stretch included an 8-0 run over 52 seconds that saw three-pointers from the Hoosiers’ Bryce Lindsay and Markus Burton. Alex Wilkins responded with five points to give the Cats a 38-30 lead with 7:25 left in the first half. Kentucky was keeping it close, but where Indiana stayed in front was on offensive rebounding. Then again, it helps to have Milan Momcilovic. The best shooter in the country exploded late in the first half, sparking a 10-0 run with back-to-back three-pointers that tied the game 45-45 with 1:25 remaining. Momcilovic was explosive in the first half, scoring 22 points and hitting five-of-six three-pointers. He was 8-10 from the floor overall, and he also dished out two assists. Zoom Diallo hit a short jumper with seven seconds remaining to give Kentucky a 47-45 lead at halftime. With 10 points, Diallo was Kentucky’s other double-digit scorer in the first half. Kentucky finished the first half 20-35 from the field and 6-10 from three-point range. They had eight assists to just two turnovers. Indiana shot 44.4 percent from the floor but missed 10 of their last 11 shots. They also went the final 3:40 of the first half without scoring. The Hoosiers were 8-18 from three-point range. While they won the rebound battle 18-14, they had three turnovers to their eight assists. Second Half Indiana came out firing in the second half, with Aiden Sherrell making back-to-back three-pointers to put the Hoosiers back up by two possessions at 5

item.title: 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan drops ‘awesome’ reaction to viral Mac Jones video
item.description: Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan drops ‘awesome’ reaction to viral Mac Jones video appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Kyle Shanahan has an all-time great coaching battle against Brian Flores coming up in Week 11 with the 49ers set to host the Vikings in Mexico City. The NFC playoff picture looks clear now with the 49ers in the driver’s seat, trailed closely by Minnesota, Detroit and Chicago in the NFC North and the Seahawks further down in the West. Ahead of Week 11’s Mexico City clash, Kyle Shanahan took a break from serious stuff to discuss Mac Jones ’ viral boombox walkout video. Mac Jones went viral this week for his 49ers boombox walkout vibe, but it's not the first time he's made waves. Jones went to the front last season w/ ex-Pats teammate Kendrick Bourne. Now Deebo is back. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In January: "I wanted to be at the front, and they wanted me to be there." pic.twitter.com/XBX7EFgvv7 — David Lombardi (@LombardiHimself) November 20, 2026 He said he liked the video according to 49ers blogger Coach Yac on X. “Yeah I saw that. My kids sent it to me. It was awesome, but that’s how we see Mac every day. If you just saw it once, you’d be like, ‘Who’s this corny white dude?’ But you don’t see it at all because he is like that all the time. He is always upbeat. He is always having fun.” The 49ers’ backup QB has appeared in two games this season but hasn’t recorded a stat. He is one of the NFL’s unquestioned top backup quarterbacks after a 2,000-plus yard, 13-touchdown season with the 49ers in 11 games in 2025 and is a former first round pick. Jones got a positive comment from Trent Williams on his off-field impact recently. The 49ers are a true team in every sense of the word, and Jones’ presence is a big reason why. item.title: 'They should be willing to flip-flop': Mike Florio suggests Thanksgiving flex games
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images, NBC Sports Next week’s slate of NFL games on Thanksgiving has a lot to like about it. In keeping with tradition, the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys will both host a game on Turkey Day, while the third, rotating primetime game will be hosted by the Buffalo Bills. But it’s possible that one aspect of the traditional Thanksgiving Day schedule is due for a change. The Lions are always the early game on Thanksgiving, while the Cowboys kickoff around 4:30 p.m. ET. The simplest reason behind this fact is time zones, but because of the relative state of both teams and the importance of their upcoming games next Thursday, Mike Florio believes the time may be right for the NFL to embrace flexing its schedule on the holiday. This year, the Lions host the Chicago Bears in a game that will have huge ramifications in the NFC North, the best division in football by a healthy margin so far this season. The Cowboys, whose defense can’t do anything, are hosting the Philadelphia Eagles, who can’t do anything on either side of the ball. While that NFC East matchup was an easy sell on paper before the start of the season, it sure looks a lot less appealing now than it did in Week 1. Florio has high expectations for the Lions-Bears game, even if it is going to start early. “I think the ratings for that game are going to be through the roof. I’m starting to think it might even be larger than the 47.7 million from last year,” Florio said, referencing the massive rating the Lions brought in with their Thanksgiving game against the Packers in 2025. “People are going to appreciate the fact that the good game is the early game. The middle game, Eagles-Cowboys, who cares? If you want to see a good, compelling, dramatic football game, that’s the one. It used to be the other way around. How many years was the Lions game just, ‘That’s what’s on TV — somebody is rolling into Detroit to beat up the Lions, it’s going to be 23–6 in the fourth quarter, let’s just get this thing over with and let’s bring out the Cowboys’? The vibe has completely shifted.” Florio argued that given the league’s broad flex privileges when it comes to its primetime schedule, a similar ability should be established to allow the league to move the better Thanksgiving game into the afternoon slot. “Frankly, they flex everything else. They should be willing to flip-flop the Lions and Cowboys games. They should be willing to say, ‘Alright we’re starting the Cowboys game at basically 12:30 p.m. ET, and we’re going to delay the Lions game.’ You give people a week, two weeks notice. We would’ve known a week or two ago that Bears-Lions is the far more compelling game. If you want to blow out the number at 4:30 p.m. ET, you put Bears-Lions in that window.” The ratings for Bears-Lions on Thanksgiving will be through the roof. They’d be even bigger if the kickoff times for Bears-Lions and Eagles-Cowboys were flipped. https://t.co/LNn9rliQBn — PFT Live (@PFT_Live) November 19, 2026 W

item.title: Sandpapergate peace deal: AUS players' union chief urges shared responsibility, slams 'unacceptable' hounding of Pat Cummins
item.description: Sandpapergate peace deal: AUS players' union chief urges shared responsibility, slams 'unacceptable' hounding of Pat Cummins originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Australian Players’ Union boss Paul Marsh wants everyone linked to the 2018 tour to share blame. He also says the intrusion into Pat Cummins’ private life has gone too far. Marsh believes a shared acknowledgement could help the sport heal and move on. Paul Marsh calls on Pat Cummins and Cricket Australia to take collective responsibility to end Sandpapergate crisis A peace deal of sorts for the Sandpapergate saga is what Paul Marsh, the chief executive of the Australian Cricketers’ Association (ACA), is now proposing. He wants every member of the 2018 touring group in South Africa, Pat Cummins and the other fast bowlers included, to stand alongside Cricket Australia (CA) and accept collective responsibility for what happened. He has stayed in regular contact with Cummins, Usman Khawaja and other players and support staff from that period, former coach Darren Lehmann among them. Out of those conversations, Marsh has concluded that an admission of shared accountability offers the group its best chance of moving forward, even if some of those on the tour continue to deny any specific knowledge of sandpaper. The proposal arrives at a delicate moment, since the dispute over who knew what, and when, has split opinion inside the game and raised awkward questions about the Australian captain himself. The current tension traces back to 2021, when Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon put their names to a joint statement, where they insisted that they had no prior knowledge of sandpaper being “taken onto the field”. Cummins has since doubled down on his position, and he now says he had no knowledge of any ball tampering, either before the tour or during it. Those claims have now been challenged by Khawaja, David Warner, Chadd Sayers and Cameron Bancroft, and their accounts have fed a growing credibility problem for Australian cricket. The situation is made more sensitive by the ACA’s own makeup, because Khawaja is a current director of the body that Marsh leads. Cummins is a former director, and so is his manager, Neil Maxwell. More to follow...

item.title: Nets shake up everything but the outcome in heartbreaking fourth straight loss
item.description: Nets magic Team meetings. Lineup changes. Whatever it took. Brooklyn tried everything to shake up a three-game losing skid. The Nets finally showed some heart Friday night. But then they got it broken in a 113-111 loss to the Magic in front of a crowd of 17,067 at Barclays Center. Franz Wagner hit a go-ahead 14-footer with 2.8 seconds left, and Julius Randle missed a desperation 3-pointer at the buzzer on the other end. Brooklyn Nets forward Danny Wolf shoots as Orlando Magic center Wendell Carter Jr. defends on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, N.Y. Robert Sabo for NY Post Randle finished with a team-high 27 points, and Brooklyn fought. They just couldn’t quite close. After the Nets (3-12) embarrassed themselves in Wednesday’s 137-107 non-effort against Chicago , they held a team meeting, with some real talk about what went wrong and how to fix it. Friday’s effort showed it wasn’t all just talk. It just wasn’t quite enough. “No one wants to lose like we did [Wednesday] … so a lot needed to be said. A lot of guys have been doing a lot of talking; we’ve all been doing a lot of talking,” Michael Porter Jr. said. “We’ve gotta string some games together. We’ve had spurts of good responses after really bad games, but that has to be a consistent theme. We can’t just let that be responses to really bad losses.” Wednesday qualified as a really bad loss, the worst of a disappointing season. Brooklyn Nets forward Julius Randle (30) goes up for a shot against the Orlando Magic at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, N.Y., Friday, Nov. 20, 2026. Robert Sabo for NY Post After that, the Nets had a look-in-the-mirror meeting that sources said included not only players, but also coaches. “Everybody collectively. It was a good conversation, and everybody pitched into what they saw,” Porter said. “There was a lot of internal discussion that I’ll keep between the team. But just realizing we got to be better and addressing what needed to be addressed.” One thing that coach Jordi Fernández did was shuffle his rotations. Orlando Magic forward Franz Wagner dunks during the second quarter against the Brooklyn Nets on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, N.Y. Robert Sabo for NY Post Egor Dëmin — last year’s lottery pick — was pulled out of the starting lineup. He was brought off the bench for the first time since Nov. 5, 2025, his rookie season. Instead, Fernández went with 6-foot-11 forward Danny Wolf as a jumbo shooting guard . And the move paid immediate dividends. Wolf poured in 20 points and five rebounds, finishing a team-high plus-15. Rookie Mikel Brown Jr. added a career-high-tying 18 points. Porter, who admitted not having the right energy in his five-point, 1-of-7 effort Wednesday, bounced back well. His layup off a Day’Ron Sharpe feed gave the Nets a 63-62 edge coming out of the half. The Nets coughed up 10 unanswered Orlando points, the run capped by Wagner (game-high 35 points). item.title: F1 qualifying results: Las Vegas Grand Prix
item.description: (Photo by Guido De Bortoli/LAT Images) George Russell led the way in the third and final hour of practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix Friday evening. But will the Mercedes driver top the timing sheets during the all-important qualifying hour later tonight? Russell led teammate Kimi Antonelli and McLaren’s Lando Norris in FP3 Friday evening, with the veteran Mercedes driver posting a lap of 1:34.041, almost a full second ahead of Antonelli, who was 0.911 seconds off the pace. Charles Leclerc and Franco Colapinto rounded out the top five. Friday’s FP3 session was the only representative session of the weekend so far, as both FP1 and FP2 on Thursday were compromised by wet weather. The biggest story so far in Las Vegas might just be the list of drivers taking a grid penalty due to new components. Five drivers — Antonelli, Lance Stroll, Oliver Bearman, Oscar Piastri, and Carlos Sainz — have already taken on new components ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix and are facing grid drops at the start of the race. Antonelli is facing a five-place grid drop, while Stroll, Piastri, and Sainz are facing ten-place grid drops. Bearman, who is taking on a fifth Internal Combustion Engine, turbocharger, exhaust, and MGU-K, and as those components all exceed the permitted amount per season, he will start at the back of the grid. But who will take pole position? We will find out soon enough. Qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix gets rolling at 11:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Friday night, so check back early and often for updates! And as always, download the new SB Nation app , join the F1 Community, and follow the qualifying thread live! item.title: Michael Strahan Names Giants Legend the True MVP of Super Bowl XLII Over Eli Manning Ahead of Netflix’s ‘Untold’ Documentary
item.description: Fox Sports Media Day, New Orleans, Louisiana, USA Former Football player and TV host Michael Strahan During the Fox Sports Media Day at the New Orleans Convention Center in New Orleans, Louisiana, USA Copyright: xMartyxJean-Louisx ©IMAGO/Marty Jean Louis Former New York Giants defensive end Justin Tuck had a picture-perfect career in the NFL. He played nine seasons with the New York Giants, where he won two Super Bowl rings, made two Pro Bowls, and was named first-team All-Pro. Yet for his teammate, former New York Giants defensive end Michael Strahan, Tuck missed one accolade that left his resume short of being perfect. To Strahan, Tuck deserved that honor, which was handed to quarterback Eli Manning. “One thing I will say, and I love him. We had him on the podcast. I love my guy Eli Manning. But this right here is the MVP of Super Bowl 42. I love Eli,” Strahan shared on the Hustle Like You’re Broke podcast. “Made some great plays. They did. They shot the second one, but the first one was right here because I’m rushing and I’m thinking I’m doing good. I’m like, I’m quick. I’m like, how the hell did they get there already? So, [laughter] he, but he had the diversity that I didn’t have to play inside and outside. “And I think that’s the one thing that he may not give himself enough credit for is it’s two totally different positions. So, to be able to switch your mind and have a body that you can do those things in is amazing. But also when you’re the guy and you got two or three guys every play hitting you, it completely changed the way football looks to you.” In Super Bowl XLII, New York’s Super Bowl hopes appeared to be hanging by a thread when Manning launched a desperate pass on third-and-5 near midfield with the Giants trailing by four. It was the kind of throw that could easily have resulted in an interception and ended the game. David Tyree somehow came up with it, trapping the ball against his helmet. The spectacular effort kept the Giants’ championship hopes alive. Strahan's surprising MVP take on the Giants' greatest moment challenges everything you thought you knew about that legendary Super Bowl run. Subscribe for the untold stories reshaping NFL history. That catch gave Manning another opportunity to lead his team downfield, and the quarterback made it count. He delivered a touchdown pass to Plaxico Burress. However, Strahan believes that Tuck also stood out by having two sacks in the Super Bowl XLII. Yet the award went to Manning. After all, Tuck also created another opportunity by forcing a Brady fumble that Osi Umenyiora recovered. The story repeated in Super Bowl XLVI. New England’s offense had been one of the most productive units in the NFL throughout the 2011 season, averaging 32.1 points per game. However, the Patriots managed just 17 against the Giants, with Tuck playing a major role in keeping Brady and company under pressure. His two sacks, three tackles, and three quarterback hits might not fully capture the impact he had

item.title: Four takeaways from Virginia’s 103-61 win against Loyola MD
item.description: The undefeated Virginia Cavaliers (7-0) secured a 42-point win over the Loyola Maryland Greyhounds (1-5) on Friday night. The 103-61 victory was not unexpected, but these non-conference games give an early look into the team’s potential for the season. Based on Friday’s 100-point game, Virginia’s crystal ball is looking pretty bright. Here are my four takeaways from the statement win. The ’Hoos have a leader in Sam Lewis With 20 points in only 24 minutes, it’s fair to say Sam Lewis didn’t waste a second on the floor. He executed along the three-point line, had a few drives to the basket, and in the first half, had a steal that led to his fast-break dunk. He tallied four rebounds, four assists, and 2 steals and went 3-of-5 from deep. He’s playing a 360-degree game, orchestrating the offense, containing his man on D, and playing a critical role in the team’s energy. He and Chance Mallory make up one of Virginia’s most dangerous pairings. Mallory’s 10 points and six assists were the perfect complement. With the two of them regularly on the floor together, the offense is anything but stale. Loyola shot well, but it was no competition for No. 4 Virginia If you look at the score, the ’Hoos dominated. And while the game itself didn’t feel like much of a competition for Virginia, they didn’t necessarily shut down Loyola’s offense. The Greyhounds shot 44% from three and 39% overall. Plus, they hit a perfect 8-of-8 from the line. If it weren’t for their 18 turnovers, you could say Loyola played a solid game. But that speaks to just how good Virginia really is. Putting up 61 points isn’t a lack of offense on Loyola’s part. But Virginia’s defense, specifically their 14 steals, limited Greyhound possessions. And of course, the ’Hoos were efficient on their own end of the court, leaving the Greyhounds in the dust. Virginia’s playing unselfish ball — and the bench contributed Virginia’s continued to build on their unselfish play. I’d credit it to good coaching as much as I would a returning roster. There’s an undeniable chemistry on the floor. They just didn’t miss a beat. Virginia displayed textbook ball movement. Four of their five starters scored double digits, and the bench contributed 40 points to the win, including Martin Carrere and Jan Vide with eight apiece. That balance matters when a starter like Johann Grünloh comes into the night 1-of-14 from three. He finally landed one on Friday, but the team’s overall performance can make up for a starter’s slump. But it’s not just on offense. Virginia’s man-to-man defense is so effective because of their solid help. The help isn’t half-baked. The bigs are quickly sliding into the double team on the block long enough to disrupt the offense; the help on the drive isn’t exposing the lane or leaving the weak side vulnerable; there’s no hesitation defending the pick. item.title: Corning advances to state volleyball final; Candor falls just short
item.description: Corning bounced back from a loss in its opener to win its final two matches Friday, Nov. 20, securing a berth in the New York State Public High School Athletic Association Class AAA girls volleyball championship match at Harding Mazzotti Arena in Glens Falls. The Section 4 champion Hawks (17-0) will face Section 2's Shenendehowa for the title at 6:30 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21. Live coverage will be available on NFHS Network , a pay service. Shenendehowa ended up with a 3-0 record in Friday's pool-play semifinals, followed by Corning at 2-1, Section 5's Rochester Mercy at 1-2, and Section 11's Bay Shore at 0-3. Shenendehowa topped Corning, 25-21, 25-21, to begin pool play. The Hawks responded with a 26-24, 25-19 victory over Bay Shore. Corning then clinched its spot in the final with a 25-21, 25-20 victory over Mercy. Corning is seeking its first state title in volleyball. Corning West won the Class B state championship in 1997, when there were only four classes instead of the current six. Corning East and Corning West combined all athletic teams in 2010. More: Corning gets shot at three-time defending state champions Candor lost out on state final on tiebreaker Candor, the only other Section 4 team to make it to the state semifinals, matched Corning's 2-1 pool-play record Friday but lost out on a spot in the Class D championship match on a tiebreaker. Candor, Section 5's York, and Section 3's Hamilton all finished with 2-1 records. The tiebreaker came down to winning percentage. Hamilton went 5-2, defending state champion York was 5-3, and Candor finished at 4-3. Hamilton beat Candor, 26-24, 25-19, in the opening match. Candor followed with a 21-25, 25-23, 15-11 victory over York, and a 25-15, 25-18 win over Section 2's Duanesburg. Hamilton and York play for the title at 4 p.m. Saturday. item.title: ‘Life is Too Short,’ ‘I Wish Him Nothing But the Best’ — Stephen A. Smith Addresses LeBron James Feud in Exchange With Skip Bayless
item.description: ‘Life is Too Short,’ ‘I Wish Him Nothing But the Best’ — Stephen A. Smith Addresses LeBron James Feud in Exchange With Skip Bayless Skip Bayless asked Stephen A. Smith on Friday’s episode of ESPN’s “First Take” whether he had mended his relationship with Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James. Smith said he had not, making clear that the two had not formally reconciled. The question brought their public feud back into focus, nearly two years after the four-time NBA MVP confronted Smith courtside over his criticism of his son, Bronny James. Stephen A. Smith Explains Where He Stands With LeBron James After Their Feud Smith addressed Bayless’ question directly before explaining why he sees little reason to hold on to the disagreement. “I’m 59 years old, bro. Life is too short. I ain’t got time to be enemies with nobody,” Smith said. “I got a job to do. I wish him nothing but the best.” The disagreement began with Smith’s criticism of James’ involvement in his son’s development with the Los Angeles Lakers. On Jan. 29, 2025, Smith questioned why the veteran superstar was pushing for Bronny to remain in the NBA rather than spend more time developing in the G League. The Lakers’ 2024 second-rounder had just gone scoreless on 0-for-5 shooting in a loss to the 76ers. Smith’s comments eventually led to a courtside confrontation during the Lakers’ game against the New York Knicks on March 6. James approached Smith and told him to stop talking about his son. The sports media personality talked about the encounter in his show the following morning, acknowledging that the 22-time All-Star had confronted him as a father protecting his child. “That wasn’t a basketball player confronting me. That was a parent. That was a father,” Smith said. James later explained his side on “The Pat McAfee Show” on March 26. He said he had no issue with analysts criticizing players’ performances but objected when the discussion became personal. “Never would I ever not allow people to talk about the sport, criticize players about what they do on the court,” James said . “But when you take it, and you get personal with it, it’s my job to not only protect my damn household but protect the players.” Smith revisited the confrontation in April 2026 during an appearance on Logan Paul’s “Impaulsive” podcast. He described James’ approach as “very disrespectful” and said he felt James had wrongly assumed his criticism of Bronny was intended to get at him. SEE ALSO: ‘All-Time Melodramatic Flopper’ – Skip Bayless Rips LeBron James After 76ers Star’s Viral Airball The ESPN star has since said he no longer holds a grudge against James.On Friday, he reiterated that he does not hate James and wants to cover the final stretch of his NBA career without carrying the dispute forward. He also expressed hope that the 41-year-old forward would win a championship with Philadelphia. James and the 76ers entered Friday at 13-3, tied for the best record in the NBA. item.description: Wisconsin men’s basketball’s humbling 70-53 loss to Murray State was not the only bad news for the Badgers in the Bahamas. Janicki also missed the last nine games of the 2025-26 season with a wrist injury. He had hoped to return during the postseason , but the Badgers’ first-round exit did not give a long enough runway for a return. His latest injury leaves the Badgers without a key defensive player and veteran presence as they try to bounce back from humbling losses to Seton Hall and Murray State in the Baha Mar Championship. “I assume we’ll be down one for the foreseeable future in Janicki, but we’ve got to have upperclassmen that have been through the fire here at Wisconsin step up and help some of these new guys.” This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: Wisconsin guard Jack Janicki suffers foot injury that 'doesn't look good'

item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. And the club dealt with a number of injuries during the course of the season, while also playing much of the year without one of its top scorers, Alonso Martinez, as he recovered from a torn ACL he suffered last fall. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.) item.title: How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊
item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
